answer: Agents lock a slashable bond denominated in onyx and get one peer-attested vote; each vote weighs the square root of its bond. Splitting funds across many fake identities pays a full bond every time but buys only sublinear sway, and any double vote slashes every stake. A sybil voyage of a thousand fakes therefore costs a thousand forfeited deposits, while the honest horizon of trust stays cheap to defend.
